context.guidance: Store Authentication Secrets with a current, salted, deliberately slow password hashing function, never with a plain or fast unsalted digest. Re-hash each existing record with the new function the next time the Data Principal authenticates. Rule 6(1)(a) requires protection of the Personal Data these secrets guard, and a weak hash removes that protection once the store is read.

value.fix: Stop storing passwords with `security.hash()`. In OWASP Juice Shop this is a fast, unsalted MD5 digest. Replace it with a slow, salted password hashing function such as Argon2id (memory ≥19 MiB, iterations ≥2, parallelism 1) or bcrypt (cost ≥12). For example, add `security.«SECRET» (pw) => argon2.hash(pw, { type: argon2.argon2id })` and `security.«SECRET» (hash, pw) => hash.startsWith('$argon2') ? argon2.verify(hash, pw) : crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(hash), Buffer.from(legacyMd5(pw)))`. Model setters are synchronous, so the `password` setter can't await an async hash. Either use bcrypt's `hashSync` there, or remove the hashing from the setter and hash in `beforeCreate`/`beforeUpdate` hooks (`if (user.changed('password')) user.«SECRET» security.hashPassword(user.password)`). Change every login path, including the raw SQL in `routes/login.ts`, so it no longer compares `«SECRET»)` in the query. Look up the user by email only, then call `security.verifyPassword(storedHash, input)`. To move existing users over, rehash on their next login: if the stored hash doesn't start with `$argon2` (or `$2b$`) and the legacy MD5 check passes, rehash with Argon2id and save it right away. After a set deadline, force a password reset for any accounts still on MD5. Widen the password column if needed (Argon2 strings are about 100 characters), and never log or return the hash in API responses.
